name: BARE1/BARE2 genomic amplification with LS1 + AP4
element: BARE1 (BARE-1) Ty1/copia-group LTR retrotransposon; gag-PR region, element-internal
citation: Chang W, Jääskeläinen M, Li S-P, Schulman AH. BARE retrotransposons are translated and replicated via distinct RNA pools. PLoS One. 2013;8(8):e72270. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0072270. PMID 23940808; PMCID PMC3735527.
where_in_paper: Primer sequences: supplementary Table S1 'Primer list' (pone.0072270.s002.pdf), rows LS1 and AP4, which also give the matching regions IN ACCESSION Z17327 (LS1 3234-3258 F; AP4 4508-4486 R). Amplicon size: Figure 1 legend - 'The upper band (arrow, 1.3 kb) contains products from both BARE1 and BARE2 and is the same size as the amplification product from genomic DNA using the same primer pair (B)'. NOTE: the paper prints only a kb-scale gel estimate ('1.3 kb'); no bp integer is stated anywhere.
amplicon_range_bp: Paper states '1.3 kb' (gel). Templated footprint on Z17327 = 3234..4508 = 1275 bp; adding the 11-nt (LS1) and 17-nt (AP4) non-templated 5' tails gives a 1303 bp full product. Accept 1275-1303 depending on whether the engine counts 5' tails.
caveats: (1) 5' TAILS: neither primer anneals over its full length. LS1's templated core is the 25-nt ACCGGACTTGAGCTAGTGGAATTGG (matches Z17327 3234-3258 exactly, as the table states); AP4's is the 22-nt ATATAATGTTCATGCTYAACGC (matches 4487-4508). A full-length exact-match search returns NO product - this case is specifically useful for testing 3'-anchored / tailed-primer handling. (2) The table's AP4 coordinate 4486 is off by one: a 23-nt core was tested and fails because Z17327 position 4486 is T, not C. (3) DEGENERATE: AP4 carries (TC) = Y at one position. (4) MULTI-LOCUS BY DESIGN: BARE1 is present at ~10^4 copies in barley, and the paper states the pair amplifies BARE2 equally well - but no exact core site exists in the BARE2 accession AJ279072, so exact matching finds the amplicon only in Z17327. (5) Size is an approximate gel estimate, hence medium confidence.
loci_justification: BARE1 is present at roughly 10^4 copies in the barley genome and the source states the pair amplifies BARE2 equally well, so the named band is the one the authors chose to report rather than the only product. A product count is not a specificity result for this assay.

name: Atlantic salmon GAPDH TaqMan reference-gene assay
element: Non-TE control assay. Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) evaluated as a real-time RT-PCR reference gene.
citation: Olsvik PA, Lie KK, Jordal AEO, Nilsen TO, Hordvik I. Evaluation of potential reference genes in real-time RT-PCR studies of Atlantic salmon. BMC Mol Biol. 2005;6:21. doi:10.1186/1471-2199-6-21. PMID 16293192; PMCID PMC1314898.
where_in_paper: Table 1 ("TaqMan assays used to evaluate potential reference genes in Atlantic salmon"), row GAPDH: "Forward primer" and "Reverse primer" columns, and 96 in the "Amplicon size (bp)" column. The template accession is given in Methods, "Design of PCR primers and TaqMan probes": "The mRNA sequences encoding S20 ribosomal protein and GAPDH were obtained from GenBank accession numbers BG936672 and BU693999, respectively (exon-exon borders were not considered)." The same section states "Amplified PCR products of all actual cDNAs were sequenced to ensure that the correct mRNA sequences were quantified."
caveats: ASSAY FORMAT: this is a TaqMan assay; the internal MGB probe (CTGATCATTGGAAACCT, Table 1) sits inside the amplicon and does not affect the 96 bp primer-to-primer product. SPLICING: the paper explicitly states exon-exon borders "were not considered" when designing the S20 and GAPDH assays, so 96 bp is established on this cDNA/EST template only - whether the primers also amplify from genomic DNA, and at what size, is simply NOT established by the paper (this is different from a known intron-spanning assay). TEMPLATE: BU693999.1 is an Atlantic salmon eye cDNA library EST (796 bp), i.e. cDNA, not genomic. In-silico check: forward matches once at 230, reverse site once ending at 325; product 230..325 = 96 bp, exact, no alternative products.

name: Atlantic salmon elongation factor 1A-A (EF1AA) TaqMan reference-gene assay
element: Non-TE control assay. Elongation factor 1 alpha paralogue A (EF1AA) evaluated as a real-time RT-PCR reference gene.
citation: Olsvik PA, Lie KK, Jordal AEO, Nilsen TO, Hordvik I. Evaluation of potential reference genes in real-time RT-PCR studies of Atlantic salmon. BMC Mol Biol. 2005;6:21. doi:10.1186/1471-2199-6-21. PMID 16293192; PMCID PMC1314898.
where_in_paper: Table 1 ("TaqMan assays used to evaluate potential reference genes in Atlantic salmon"), row EF1AA: "Forward primer" and "Reverse primer" columns, and 57 in the "Amplicon size (bp)" column. Template accession in Methods, "Design of PCR primers and TaqMan probes": "The EF1A A assay was based on a cDNA clone that we reported to the GenBank previously (AF321836)". The same paragraph states "The primers amplify PCR products between 57-98 basepairs (bp) long".
caveats: ASSAY FORMAT: TaqMan; internal MGB probe ATCGGTGGTATTGGAAC lies inside the amplicon and does not change the 57 bp primer-to-primer product. SPLICING - IMPORTANT AND DIFFERENT FROM THE GAPDH CASE: these primers FLANK an intron. The paper states the exon-exon borders were deduced by alignment with zebrafish and that "The chosen primers were subsequently used to confirm that the salmon genes contained an intron between the same sites... The PCR products containing the introns were cloned into TOPO vector and sequenced." So on genomic DNA this pair yields 57 bp PLUS the intron; the 57 bp ground truth applies to cDNA/mRNA template (AF321836.1, "Salmo salar elongation factor 1 alpha mRNA, complete cds", 1445 bp). SIZE: at 57 bp this is the short-amplicon end of the set. In-silico check: forward matches once at 800, reverse site once ending at 856; product 800..856 = 57 bp, exact, no alternative products. EF1A is a two-paralogue system in salmon (EF1AA/EF1AB); the EF1AB assay in the same table uses a different, overlapping primer pair, so cross-paralogue priming should be considered if the engine is run against a whole-transcriptome target rather than this single accession.
